title: You Have a Role in the Story — 1 Peter 4:10
paragraphs: You Have a Role in the Story — 1 Peter 4:10
You were never saved to sit still.
He gave you something.

Not for display.
Not for ego.
Not for hiding.
For service.
“As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God’s varied grace.” — 1 Peter 4:10
That verse crushes two lies at once.

The first lie says, “I have nothing to offer.”
The second says, “What I have is mine.”
But Peter says each has received a gift.
Each.

Not just pastors.
Not just singers.
Not just the loud, polished, platform-ready people.
You have a role in the story God is writing.

Maybe your gift is preaching.
Maybe it is mercy.
Maybe it is generosity when nobody sees.
Maybe it is encouragement that keeps a weary soul from quitting.
Maybe it is serving quietly, praying fiercely, giving faithfully, loving deeply.
And here’s what we miss:

Your gift is not proof that you are great.
Your gift is proof that God is gracious.

A steward does not own the treasure.
He carries it carefully.
He uses it for the Master’s purpose.

That means the real tragedy is not being untalented.
The real tragedy is burying what God gave you out of fear, pride, comparison, or distraction.

Some of us are waiting for a bigger stage.
But heaven is watching what we do with today’s assignment.

Use your gift.
Use your voice.
Use your hands.
Use your story.
Use your pain redeemed by Christ.
Because the Church is weakened when believers stay spectators.
And this points us straight to Jesus.

He is not only the Giver of the gift.
He is the Savior who rescues broken, self-centered people and makes them useful by grace.
At the cross, Christ paid for our selfishness, our laziness, our pride, our excuses.
In His resurrection, He gives new life, new purpose, and a place in His mission.

So no, you are not random.
And no, your part is not small when it is surrendered to God.

Serve with what He gave you.
Not to be seen.
But so Christ will be seen.

You have a role in the story.
Play it for the glory of the King.
